Unit 11 Quiz: Skills That Survive

Test your understanding of the four durable PMM skills

Question 1 of 8 0/8 correct
Question 1 of 8
According to the unit, what is the key distinction between the PMM of 2023 and the PMM of 2028?

✓ Correct!

The shift is from execution (producing deliverables) to judgment (making decisions agents can't make). Deliverables still get produced, but the human's contribution shifts from drafting to directing.

✗ Not quite

The key distinction is that the 2023 PMM spent majority time on execution (producing deliverables), while the 2028 PMM will spend majority time on judgment (making decisions agents can't make).

Question 2 of 8
What are the four surviving skills that define the agentic-era PMM?

✓ Correct!

These four meta-skills cut across multiple PMM activities and represent capabilities that agents can't replicate—they become MORE valuable as routine work is automated.

✗ Not quite

The four surviving skills are: Strategic Judgment, Organizational Intelligence, Narrative Craft, and Customer Empathy. These are meta-skills that agents can't replicate.

Question 3 of 8
Which surviving skill is described as "the one AI is furthest from replicating"?

✓ Correct!

Organizational intelligence—navigating stakeholders, reading body language, understanding informal power structures, having the coffee conversations that reveal real objections—is uniquely human work that no agent can replicate.

✗ Not quite

Organizational Intelligence is the skill AI is furthest from replicating. No agent can have the informal coffee conversations, read body language, or navigate the political dynamics that determine what actually gets done.

Question 4 of 8
What's the key difference between "customer knowledge" and "customer empathy"?

✓ Correct!

Agents can provide comprehensive customer knowledge (usage patterns, NPS scores, feature requests). Customer empathy is understanding the frustration of budget approval battles, the anxiety of betting your reputation on a vendor choice, the relief when something actually works.

✗ Not quite

Customer knowledge is data (usage patterns, support tickets, NPS). Customer empathy is understanding feelings—the frustration, anxiety, and relief that customers experience. That's why "Stop dreading Monday's forecast meeting" hits differently than "Improve forecast accuracy by 34%."

Question 5 of 8
In the T-Shaped PMM model, what does the horizontal bar represent?

✓ Correct!

The horizontal bar is broad agent fluency—the ability to direct agents for CI, content, data analysis, launch coordination. Every PMM needs this bar as minimum table stakes for the agentic era.

✗ Not quite

The horizontal bar represents broad competence across agent-augmented skills—CI, content, data analysis, launch coordination. It's table stakes: the minimum agent fluency required to remain competitive.

Question 6 of 8
What are the three components of Narrative Craft?

✓ Correct!

Story Selection is knowing which story to tell when. Specificity is using concrete details (named people, specific numbers). Voice is the quality that makes your writing recognizably yours—not tics, but authentic expression.

✗ Not quite

The three components are: Story Selection (matching stories to arguments), Specificity (concrete details rather than abstract claims), and Voice (authentic expression that makes your writing recognizably yours).

Question 7 of 8
According to the positioning example in the unit, why does "Stop dreading Monday's forecast meeting" work better than "Improve forecast accuracy by 34%"?

✓ Correct!

This is the difference between knowledge-based positioning (features mapped to requirements) and empathy-based positioning (capabilities mapped to emotions). The second connects with the felt experience of daily work life.

✗ Not quite

The empathy-based positioning works because it connects with the human experience—what bad forecasting actually feels like in a planning team's daily life. It maps capabilities to emotions, not just features to requirements.

Question 8 of 8
What makes someone a "10x PMM" according to the unit?

✓ Correct!

The 10x PMM has figured out what to outsource to machines and what to keep for themselves. They have the full T-shape: broad horizontal competence in agent-augmented work PLUS deep vertical expertise in one surviving skill.

✗ Not quite

The 10x PMM has both bars of the T-shape: broad agent fluency (table stakes) AND deep expertise in one of the four surviving skills (differentiator). They've figured out what to outsource and what to keep.
